title: A morphism of simplicial sets that is bijective below n, surjective at n and coskeletal above is a trivial Kan fibration
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-section at source lines 6198-6211: for a morphism f : V -> U of simplicial sets, if f is a bijection in degrees below n, a surjection in degree n, and both V and U are isomorphic to the n-coskeleton of their n-skeleta, then f is a trivial Kan fibration. The proof at source lines 6213-6238 is a horn-filling argument that has to be run in two regimes. For a horn of dimension at most n the filling comes from the bijectivity in low degrees together with the surjectivity in degree n; for a horn of dimension greater than n the proof uses the coskeletal hypotheses to show that the relevant skeleton of the standard simplex coincides with that of its boundary, which makes the extension automatic and produces the dotted arrow. Both regimes must be treated and the statement mentions neither the skeleton computations nor the case split. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
